sites.rationale: L6 names S898 as the insertion position in ECL4. Python lookup confirms seq[897]='H' and seq[898]='S'; 'positioned at position S898' most naturally means the tag occupies that position, i.e., is inserted between H897 and S898 (insert_after_residue=897). A one-residue ambiguity exists (could be after S898), but both readings place the tag well within ECL4 (18–19 residues from TM7 end, 20–21 residues from TM8 start), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-boundary constraint. This site is 4 residues N-terminal to the validated N901 site, providing an independent, distinct junction in the same loop. Confidence is medium because no functional or surface-expression data are reported in the clip. Full-length CFTR TMD2-3HA construct generated by Gibson assembly from pBI-CMV2-CFTR with a triple-HA tag gene block positioned at S898 in ECL4. The phrasing 'positioned at position S898' indicates the tag is inserted immediately before S898, i.e., between H897 and S898 (insert_after_residue=897). The clip describes construct generation only; no downstream functional or surface-expression assay result is reported in the clip. sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface localisation confirmed by live-cell imaging in CFBE cells after doxycycline induction; L5 explicitly states the FLAG tag in ECL4 proximal to residue 901 'enables cell surface localization of CFTR without altering its expression'. Chloride channel function not directly re-assayed in these traffic-reporter studies but expression level is reported as unaltered.
sites.rationale: L1 names the junction explicitly as 'between Asn901 and Ser902', placing the tag in ECL4 (topology-landmark span 880–917). Python lookup confirms seq[901]='N' and seq[902]='S', matching the paper exactly. The site is 22 residues from the upstream TM7 boundary (end 879) and 17 residues from the downstream TM8 boundary (start 918), well clear of the ≥3-residue minimum. L4 and L5 provide independent corroboration of the same junction and confirm surface expression without expression-level perturbation, raising confidence to high. Full-length CFTR with FLAG octapeptide (DYKDDDDK) inserted between N901 and S902 in ECL4, expressed stably in CFBE airway epithelial cells via doxycycline-inducible lentiviral vector (mCherry-Flag-CFTR traffic reporter construct). L4 independently confirms FLAG after residue N901 in a lentiviral expression vector for stable cell-line generation. L5 summarises published evidence that this insertion enables cell-surface localisation without altering CFTR expression. [validation: surface_and_function; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

literature_notes: L2, L3, and L10 describe mCherry fused to the N-terminus of full-length CFTR. CFTR residue 1 is intracellular (topology landmark 1–77 = INTRACELLULAR); there is no signal peptide and no extracellular N-terminus. These clips therefore do not qualify as extracellular tag sites and were excluded. L11 and L12 describe a C-terminal GFP fusion on full-length CFTR; residue 1480 is intracellular (topology landmark 1148–1480 = INTRACELLULAR), so this is also excluded. L7 reports CRISPR/Cas9 HiBiT knock-in at 'two candidate positions' in ECL4 of endogenous CFTR but names neither position; this is region-level evidence only and does not add a new pinned site beyond those already established by L1 and L6. L8 and L9 describe HiBiT in the 'extracellular domain' of CFTR constructs 'as previously described', referencing the same prior literature as L1/L4; they provide additional support for the ECL4 region but name no new residue and therefore do not generate additional sites. ECL1 (94–124), ECL2 (219–222), ECL3 (325–347), ECL5 (1012), and ECL6 (1122–1126) are not supported by any qualifying ledger insertion and were not proposed.
